title: ReaAction
description: The one action vocabulary for REA (Resource–Event–Agent) flows: what an economic event or commitment does to a resource. The same words serve code, a co-op grocer and a community-garden network. Rival goods move by `transfer` / `transfer-custody` / `pickup` / `dropoff` (a crate of tomatoes delivered is no longer at the farm); non-rival knowledge, designs and code are `cite`d (a library a program builds on stays where it was). Aligned with ValueFlows actions (https://www.valueflo.ws/concepts/actions/) plus the protocol's own storage, doorway and review actions. Core tier = exactly the actions the elohim DNA declares in `content_store_integrity`'s hand-written `REA_ACTIONS` const; that const is never generated (generating into an integrity zome would move the DNA hash) and is instead checked against this tier by `pnpm run schema:check-dna` (see `_dnaMirror`). The remaining values are `affirm` and `dismiss`, the epistemic review verbs `elohim_epr::witness::ReaVerb` carries for witnessed interactions; every `ReaVerb` maps onto a value here (pinned by `rea_verb_maps_onto_the_generated_action_enum` in `elohim/epr/src/witness.rs`). Source of truth: this schema. The DNA const mirrors the core tier; no integrity rule validates an action against either list today, so membership here is a shared name, not an enforced gate.

core.rationale: Declared in the elohim DNA's REA_ACTIONS (content_store_integrity).

_codegen.rationale: Emitted to TypeScript (schema-enums.ts) and to the epr crate (elohim/epr/src/generated/), never to an integrity zome's generated_enums.rs. epr is upstream of epr-rea and elohim-storage, so every Rust consumer can read one list.

_dnaMirror.rationale: The DNA const is hand-written in an integrity zome and is declared, never validated, by any integrity rule. It changes only with a deliberate DNA move; check-dna holds it equal to the core tier so neither side drifts silently.
